title: SVMS: SciFlair Video Management Software
subtitle: Our own video management software for large camera networks over mixed and constrained links
headline: Our own video management software, rewritten from the ground up and proven on a 100+ camera network and in command-and-control vehicles
photoAlt: SVMS running on a control-room video wall
need: Security operators have to watch, record and control large numbers of IP cameras spread across wide areas, often over links with very different capacity: microwave, satellite, fibre, WiMax and mobile networks.

Our clients needed one system that works the same way in a fixed control room, a command-and-control vehicle or a rapidly deployed portable kit, makes the most of constrained links, and limits each operator to the cameras they are authorised to see.
role: SVMS is SciFlair's own software. Years of supporting the earlier video management software in the field showed where its bottlenecks were, so we rewrote it from the ground up with a new modular architecture. We own the architecture and code.
built: Database Server: the single point of access to the configuration database, so every other module can run on its own machine anywhere on the network
Operator GUI: up to 12 live or recorded views per monitor, a centred view with thumbnails, and pan, tilt, zoom, presets and auxiliary commands such as wipers for PTZ cameras
Relay Player: drives video walls and remote displays with no user interface, configured centrally from the GUI
Video Proxy: pulls each camera stream once over the constrained link and redistributes it locally, so more viewers do not mean more traffic on the link
File Recorder: continuous MP4 recording in two-minute segments, with search, export to external drives and import of footage from other sources
ONVIF camera discovery, with manual set-up for cameras that are not ONVIF-compliant
Administrator and operator roles, with each operator limited to the cameras assigned to them
builtScope: Deployed on fixed sites, in command-and-control vehicles and in portable kits, over microwave, satellite, fibre, WiMax and GSM links.

delivery.title: Architecture definition
delivery.text: A modular client–server architecture in which every module connects to the Database Server, so a system scales by adding recorders, proxies and wall players on separate machines.

delivery.title: Integration
delivery.text: Cameras from different manufacturers are integrated through ONVIF or manual configuration, and each is verified by assigning it to a display cell and confirming live video.

delivery.title: Proven in service
delivery.text: Deployed on the 100+ camera HD surveillance network and in mobile and portable command-and-control systems.

delivery.title: Next stage
delivery.text: The next step is to validate SVMS on current operating systems and camera models ahead of new deployments. We are looking for a partner or client to take it forward.
